content: Altretamine has the potential to reduce the number of blood cells produced in your bone marrow. It can also cause neurotoxicity. If you experience symptoms such as tingling in your hands or feet, mental confusion, or loss of coordination, contact your doctor immediately. Your doctor will conduct tests before, during, and after your treatment to monitor the effects of this drug on your blood cells. Your doctor has prescribed altretamine to help treat your illness. This medication is available in capsule form and is typically taken orally after meals and at bedtime. Altretamine is usually administered in repeated cycles, where it is taken for 14 to 21 days, followed by a 14 to 21-day break. This drug is primarily used to treat ovarian cancer, but it may also be prescribed for other conditions. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Altretamine is a derivative of s-triazine and works by slowing or halting the growth of cancer cells in your body. The duration of your treatment will depend on the specific drugs you are taking, how your body responds to them, and the type of cancer you have. Before starting altretamine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to this medication or any other drugs. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially aspirin, antidepressants, other anticancer drugs, and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have a history of seizure disorders, nervous system diseases, or blood disorders. Be aware that altretamine may disrupt the normal menstrual cycle in women and may reduce sperm production in men. However, this does not guarantee that pregnancy is impossible. Women who are pregnant or breastfeeding should inform their doctors before starting this medication. Avoid planning to have children during chemotherapy and for a period after treatment. Use a reliable method of birth control to prevent pregnancy, as altretamine can harm the fetus. Discuss further details with your doctor. Additionally, avoid consuming alcohol while taking this medication, as it may cause side effects such as stomach upset, vomiting, stomach cramps, headaches, sweating, and facial flushing. Common side effects of altretamine include loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, and weakness. If you experience severe or prolonged fatigue, inform your doctor. Serious side effects requiring immediate medical attention include unusual bruising or bleeding, dizziness, fever, chills, rapid heartbeat, fainting, mood changes, sore throat, or skin rash. If you experience any serious side effects, you or your doctor can report them to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly by consulting your pharmacist. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Take altretamine exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Do not take more or less of it or take it more frequently than directed. Continue taking altretamine even if you feel well, and do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor.
